sections.heading: How JEE preparation is structured here
body: JEE rewards depth over coverage: a smaller set of chapters mastered to problem-solving level outscores a full syllabus skimmed once. Our track follows that logic — concept-first notes establish each chapter's results and standard techniques, chapter-wise PYQs show how the examiners actually test them, and graded practice sets bridge the gap between board-level comfort and Advanced-level thinking.

Physics leans on mechanics as the grammar of everything after it; Chemistry splits into NCERT-anchored Inorganic, logic-driven Organic and practice-heavy Physical; Mathematics compounds — weak algebra quietly caps calculus scores. The subject pages call out these dependencies so study order is never a guess.

sections.heading: Using PYQs the JEE way
body: JEE previous year questions are training data, not just assessment. Solve them topic-wise immediately after learning a chapter, tag every mistake by cause — concept gap, calculation slip, misread question — and maintain a formula-and-mistakes register that becomes the entire revision in the last month.

Mock tests enter once a subject's core is covered: one full paper a week under strict timing, analysed the same day. Score trends across mocks, not single-paper highs, tell you whether preparation is actually compounding.

sections.heading: What stays separate from school prep
body: JEE material lives in its own track with its own difficulty curve — it never mixes with Class 6–10 board resources. Board exams reward complete, well-presented answers; JEE rewards speed and option elimination. Students preparing for both should finish board-level mastery of a chapter first, then switch to this track's JEE layer for the same chapter.

faqs.question: Should I prepare for JEE alongside Class 11–12 boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in that order per chapter: board-level concepts first, then JEE problem practice. The two reinforce each other when sequenced this way.

faqs.question: How important are mock tests versus chapter practice?
faqs.answer: Chapter practice builds the weapon; mocks teach you to wield it under time pressure. Roughly 70% chapter sets and PYQs, 30% mocks through most of preparation, shifting toward mocks in the final stretch.

faqs.question: Which subject should I start with?
faqs.answer: Start with your strongest subject to build momentum and a working system — notes, PYQs, mistake register — then transplant that system to the other two.
